## Introduction

A **double category** has both: *tight* arrows (functions), *loose* arrows
(relations), and *squares* relating them. We use these to express how to **lift** programs (or functions) to specifications (or relations) of their behavior.

This is a reference for effectful programs as arrows @power97.
::::

:::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## Double categories

::: {#def-proto-double-category}
A proto double category has objects, tight arrows $f : V \to V'$, loose arrows
$M : V \larr W$ and squares

::: {.imagify}
\begin{tikzcd}
	V && W \\
	& {\Downarrow \phi} \\
	V' && W'
	\arrow["N"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["f"', from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["g", from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["N'"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
\end{tikzcd}
:::

with loose composition associative and unital up to coherent (globular) isomorphisms.

:::

::: {#def-double-category}

A double category is a proto double category which furthermore has a loose composition of squares


::: {.imagify}
[]: %
\begin{tikzcd}
	V && W && X \\
	& {\Downarrow \phi} && {\Downarrow \psi} \\
	{V'} && {W'} && {X'}
	\arrow["N"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["f"', from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["M"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-3, to=1-5]
	\arrow["g"', from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["h"', from=1-5, to=3-5]
	\arrow["{N'}"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
	\arrow["{M'}"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-3, to=3-5]
\end{tikzcd}
:::

as well as tight composition of squares

::: {.imagify}
[]: %
\begin{tikzcd}
	V && W \\
	& {\Downarrow \phi} \\
	V' && W'\\
    & {\Downarrow \phi'}\\
    V'' && W''. \\
	\arrow["N"{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["f", from=1-1, to=3-1]
	\arrow["g", from=1-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow["N'"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=3-1, to=3-3]
	\arrow["f'", from=3-1, to=5-1]
	\arrow["g'", from=3-3, to=5-3]
	\arrow["N''"'{inner sep=.8ex}, "\shortmid"{marking}, from=5-1, to=5-3]
\end{tikzcd}
:::

which satisfy the interchange law.

:::

## Examples

::: {#exm-rel}
$\rel$ has sets, functions and relations $R \subseteq A \times B$. A square
from $R$ to $R'$ along $f, g$ exists when

$$\forall (x, y) \in R.\ (f(x), g(y)) \in R'.$$

:::

::: {#exm-prfrel}

$\prfrel$ has sets, functions and proof relevant relations $R : A \larr B$ (functor $\text{Disc}(A) \times \text{Disc}(B) \rightarrow \set$). A square from $R$ to $R'$ along $f$ and $g$ is a $\phi =$

$$(\phi_{x,y} : R(x,y) \rightarrow R'(f(x),g(y)))_{(x,y) \in A \times B}.$$

:::

::: {#exm-prof}

For a symmetric monoidal category $\mathcal{V}$, $\vprof$ has $\mathcal{V}$-enriched categories, $\mathcal{V}$-enriched functors and $\mathcal{V}$-Profunctors $M : \mathbb{A}\larr \mathbb{B}$ ($\mathcal{V}$-functor $\mathbb{A} \otimes \mathbb{B}^{op} \rightarrow \mathcal{V}$). A square from $M$ to $M'$ along $F$ and $G$ is a $\mathcal{V}$-natural transformation 

$$\phi : M \Rightarrow M' \circ F \otimes G^{op}.$$

:::
